Russell M. Nelson is the current president of **The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter‑day Saints (LDS Church)**, the world’s fourth‑largest Christian denomination. ### Quick facts | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Full name** | Russell Marion Nelson | | **Born** | September 9 1924, Salt Lake City, Utah, USA | | **Profession before church leadership** | Cardiothoracic surgeon (renowned for pioneering work in open‑heart surgery, especially heart‑valve replacements) | | **Education** | B.S. in physics (University of Utah, 1945); M.D. (University of Utah School of Medicine, 1947) | | **Church service** | • Called as a **general authority** (member of the First Quorum of the Seventy) in 1984
• Served as **President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles** (2015‑2018)
• Became **President of the Church** on January 14 2018, succeeding Thomas S. Monson | | **Key initiatives as President** | • Emphasis on “home-centered, church‑supported” gospel learning
• Accelerated construction of new temples worldwide (over 50 announced in his first few years)
• Expanded use of technology for member outreach (e.g., livestreamed General Conference, online resources)
• Revisions to church policies on priesthood eligibility, temple recommend standards, and other doctrinal clarifications | | **Publications** | • *The Power of Spiritual Momentum* (2020)
• *The Correct Name of the Church* (2022)
• Numerous talks and essays compiled in official church manuals and on the church’s website | | **Personal life** | Married to Dantzel “Dantzie” (née Jensen) Nelson (married 1945; she passed away in 2022). They have five children. | ### Why he’s notable - **Medical pioneer:** Before full‑time church service, Nelson performed thousands of heart surgeries and helped develop techniques still used today. - **Spiritual leader:** As the 17th president of the LDS Church, he is considered a prophet, seer, and revelator by church members, guiding doctrinal, administrative, and humanitarian directions for a global membership of roughly 17 million people. - **Cultural impact:** His speeches and writings influence not only church members but also broader discussions on faith, family, health, and service.
